display.purpose: The story title on the stage; the largest text in the room.

count.purpose: The 3, 2, 1 that takes over the stage before a reveal.

numeral.purpose: A scorecard's value, sized at 52% of the card's width.

headline.purpose: Page titles; weight 900 inside a band.

body.purpose: Prose, fields and everything read up close. Tabular numerals.

themes.storage: localStorage key 'ay-theme' ('light' or 'dark'); browser only, applied by a nonce-carrying script in app.html before first paint; unset follows the device.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Scorecards, hand cards and the dialog, light theme. Token --shadow.

shadows.name: played
shadows.purpose: The ring round the hand card you played.

shadows.name: dock
shadows.purpose: Upper edge of the docked hand.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The one easing: card turn, count beat, hand-card lift.

motion.name: turn
motion.purpose: Every scorecard rotates 180deg about Y in one move, in unison.

motion.name: beat
motion.purpose: Each count numeral, re-created every second so it cuts in.

motion.name: sweep
motion.value: 1s linear both; scaleX 0 to 1 from the left
motion.purpose: The 0.5rem yellow line under the count, once per beat.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hand card hover (0.3rem up) and played (0.5rem up).

motion.name: ripple
motion.value: canvas; peak alpha 0.16, radius about 2 tiles, per-frame decay level * 0.94 - 0.0015
motion.purpose: Pointer ripple on the tile grid. Fine pointers only; off under reduced motion.

constraints.name: no-inline-styles
constraints.body: Content Security Policy style-src 'self': no style attributes and no Svelte transition:/in:/out:/animate: directives. Dynamic values go through the cssVar action (apps/web/src/lib/ui/cssVar.ts).

constraints.name: self-hosted
constraints.body: Fonts come from @fontsource-variable/big-shoulders and @fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next (SIL OFL). No third-party origins.

components.css: .ds-count { position: relative; overflow: hidden; margin: 0; height: 15rem; display: grid; place-items: center; background: var(--stage-deep); color: var(--stage-ink); font-family: var(--font-display, 'Big Shoulders Variable', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-weight: 900; font-size: 9rem; line-height: 1; animation: ds-beat 1s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) infinite both; } .ds-count::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 0; height: 0.5rem; width: 100%; background: var(--action); transform-origin: left; animation: ds-sweep 1s linear infinite both; } @keyframes ds-beat { from { transform: scale(1.22); } to { transform: scale(1); } } @keyframes ds-sweep { from { transform: scaleX(0); } to { transform: scaleX(1); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-count, .ds-count::after { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Estimation is judging. The interface is a judging panel at a diving meet: one field of pool aqua, the stage, carries the story being scored; below it, on a tiled floor, a row of white scorecards sits face down until every one of them turns in the same instant. The highest and lowest are flagged in red and named on the stage, because they speak first. There is no table, no ring of avatars and no illustration; the scene is made from colour fields, a square tile grid and heavy scoreboard numerals.

The system has two themes of equal standing. Light is the day session: cool white tile, dark ink. Dark is the evening final: scoreboard black, the pool deepened to a lit teal, the scorecards still white. The first visit follows the device; the toggle in the bar overrides it; the choice is kept in the browser only (`localStorage` key `ay-theme`) and applied before first paint, so no page flashes the wrong theme. Every colour decision is made twice, once per theme.

Everything apart from the stage and the cards is plain: standard web controls, one measured column for reading and forms, sections divided by a rule. The tool sits beside a meeting and must not compete with it.
keyCharacteristics: One full-bleed aqua field per page: the stage in the room, a band everywhere else.
Colour is rationed: aqua for the stage, yellow for the one next step, red for flags and deletion.
Condensed scoreboard numerals for anything that is read across a shared screen; a sturdy legible sans for everything else.
A 32px square tile grid in the ground, in the stage and, finer, on the card backs.
Motion is spent on one moment, the count and the turn. Nothing else on the page moves.
No inline styles anywhere; the Content Security Policy forbids them.

rules.name: The Three Signals Rule
rules.body: Aqua owns the stage and the bands. Yellow is the next step. Red is a flag or a deletion. None of the three is used for decoration, and none borrows another's job.

rules.name: The Moving Yellow Rule
rules.body: A screen has one yellow button, and it is whatever comes next: Reveal while voting, New round after the reveal, Create or Join on a form. The same button loses its yellow when it stops being the next step. Secondary actions on the same screen are outlined in ink.

rules.name: The Word With The Flag Rule
rules.body: Red never carries meaning alone. A flag always holds the word High or Low, and the same names are repeated in text on the stage.

rules.name: The Twice Rule
rules.body: Every colour is specified for both themes and checked in both. Contrast measured from the shipped values: body ink on ground 17:1 light and 16.5:1 dark; white on the stage 5.7:1 light and 7.4:1 dark; ink on yellow 11:1.

rules.name: The Scoreboard Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders is for things read from across the room: the story title, card numerals, the count, the timer, the verdict, headings, and the one large action button in the rail or bar (800, 1.5rem, 0.03em). It never sets a sentence of body text, a label or a field.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: There are two families and no third. Code samples and links to copy fall back to the system monospace.

rules.name: The Still Stage Rule
rules.body: The stage keeps one height through the reveal. The slot for the result is reserved before there is a result (4.25rem, or 5.25rem from 40rem wide), and the count is laid over the stage, not inserted into it. When the cards turn, nothing below the stage moves.

rules.name: The Under The Thumb Rule
rules.body: What a person does most often sits at the bottom edge: the hand for a voter, the next step for a moderator on a phone.

rules.name: The Objects Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is a card or a sheet above the page". Panels, the rail, history entries, fields and buttons are separated by a 1px line, never a shadow.

dos: Do give every screen one yellow button, and make it the next step. Move the yellow when the next step changes.
Do open every page with a full-bleed field of Pool Aqua: the stage in the room, a band elsewhere.
Do show a role as a badge after the name. A name is free text, so a role written in the same run of text could be forged by a name.
Do pair red with the word it stands for.
Do design and check both themes together; neither is the default.
Do pass dynamic values to CSS through the `cssVar` action, which sets custom properties from script, and keep every other style in a stylesheet.
Do take motion from stylesheets (`transition`, `@keyframes`) and the one canvas, and let `prefers-reduced-motion` reduce all of it.
Do reserve the space for anything that appears later (the result, a flag), so its arrival moves nothing.
Do set anything read across a shared screen in Big Shoulders at 800 or 900.
Do draw disabled buttons with a dashed border, not lowered opacity.
donts: Don't write a `style` attribute, or use Svelte's `transition:`, `in:`, `out:` or `animate:` directives. The Content Security Policy blocks inline styles and they will fail silently in production.
Don't use red for emphasis, errors of taste, or branding. It means High, Low, or "this deletes something".
Don't put a second yellow button on a screen, and don't use yellow as a background tint or highlight.
Don't seat people round a table, draw avatars, or round the cards into playing cards. The room is a row of judges with scorecards.
Don't animate anything other than the count, the card turn, the lift of a hand card and the ripple. No entrance animations, no fades between states.
Don't ease or fade the count. Each number replaces the last outright.
Don't use shadows to separate panels, fields or buttons; use a 1px line.
Don't load a font, image, script or sound from another origin. Everything is self-hosted.
Don't change the scorecard for dark mode. It is white with black numerals in both themes.
